thread:
Sanjay Patel: quick follow-up on the qkv concat path RFC — found an oddness when the dropout-free codepath is enabled
Maria Chen: what oddness?
Sanjay Patel: when we route small-batch inference to the dropoutless kernels, kv-cache rotation (seq offset) sometimes invalidates the prefix cache entries — results in higher token latency on 1/8th batches
Lee Wang: hmm that sounds like an index/stride mismatch in the concat ordering between fused-qkv and the legacy path
Jen Ortiz: can you paste the failing trace?
Sanjay Patel: stack is small, repro in unit test:
```
AssertionError: cache_mismatch at i=0 expected offset 1024 got 960
at runtime/kv_cache.cc:138
```
Kevin Liu: do we still use the old layout (Q,K,V interleaved) for fallback? I thought concat path used Q||K||V contiguous for vectorized kernels
Maria Chen: we do both depending on kernel capability flags. Kernel v2 advertises `layout=contiguous_qkv` and `dropout_capable=false`
Sanjay Patel: problem is the router sometimes falls back to kernel v1 (interleaved) mid-stream due to transient memory pressure; cache entries are written with contiguous layout then read with interleaved layout -> mismatch
Lee Wang: two actionable options: 1) add a sticky-routing SLA per request so once a request chooses a layout it sticks to compatible fallbacks, or 2) normalize cache storage to canonical layout (pick one on write) and convert on read
Jen Ortiz: sticky routing seems simpler operationally but may affect utilization. normalizing cache increases CPU overhead on every cache hit
Kevin Liu: perf numbers?
Sanjay Patel: rough microbench: sticky routing increases tail latency by ~0.5ms for small batches due to less opportunistic packing; cache-normalize adds ~0.2ms per lookup on our x86 path but less on gpu since conversion is memcopy-heavy
Maria Chen: also need to consider release complexity. Cache-normalize touches KV shapeshift and will require schema versioning in the persistence layer
Lee Wang: agree. For short-term we should do sticky routing + a monitoring counter for cross-layout fallbacks and a regression test that forces fallback mid-request
Jen Ortiz: +1. Add a config flag `router.layout_sticky=true/false` default true for 2 weeks, then flip if metrics look bad
Sanjay Patel: will draft a tiny RFC for the flag and a unit test that simulates memory-pressure fallback. also adding an e2e perf job in ci/runtime-perf that toggles `layout_sticky`
ops-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: runtime-unit-tests (linux, gpu) started by Sanjay Patel
Kevin Liu: small note: also watch fused bias+rope variants — if we canonicalize cache we must include rope-offset metadata so reads are correct when rope is applied lazily
Maria Chen: noted — add `cache.meta.rope_offset` and `cache.meta.layout` fields in the schema doc
Sanjay Patel: ok i'll push a draft RFC in `rfc/eng-runtime` and ping infra to add the perf job. thanks all :thumbsup:
Jen Ortiz: thanks. add a short blurb in the rollback playbook in case sticky routing causes unexpected cost spikes
Lee Wang: will add the playbook entry
Maria Chen: i'll own the schema change and bump the version in storage adapters
Sanjay Patel: next action items: (1) RFC + tests (Sanjay), (2) config flag in router (Kevin), (3) schema update (Maria), (4) perf job + playbook (Jen/Lee). target: ship staged change next week
Kevin Liu: ack
Maria Chen: ack
Jen Ortiz: ack
Lee Wang: ack
